name: implicit-imageblock-half4-every-pixel
rationale:
A full 16x16 single-sample tile read, incremented and written back through a four-half implicit imageblock, then read a second time into a device buffer so all 256 pixels are compared rather than one. air.load.implicit_imageblock.v4f16 and its store are 30 corpus sources and the sibling half2 fixture only ever observed a single render-target pixel.

Every pixel carries a different quadruple -- red is the column, green is the row, blue is row times sixteen plus column and alpha is a hundred plus the column -- so a transposed tile, a wrong plane index or a stride that walks the tile in the wrong order all move the answer, and the buffer read-back is indexed by the same position the imageblock was, which pins the two orders to each other. All 1024 values and all 1024 incremented values are integers at most 256, which binary16 holds exactly, so the increment and the comparison are both exact.

name: thread-elements-against-block-load-and-store-of-an-8x8-matrix
rationale: Settles the owed Metal reading behind D91.1: which cells of an 8x8 simdgroup matrix thread_elements()[0..1] hold, read against the block load and store, and that a product computed from elements written that way is the product of the stored matrix (the agx2 operand reading). One simdgroup (32 threads). Lane L writes in[2L + j] = 2L + j + 1 into element j of a; b is a block load of in[64..128) at leading dimension 8 with b[r][c] = 100 + 8r + c (every cell distinct). out[0..64) holds b's elements as lane L reads them (out[2L + j]), out[64..128) the block store of a, out[128..192) the elements of r = a * b, out[192..256) the block store of r. Under D91.1 lane L holds cell (row(L), col(L) + j) with row(L) = ((L >> 1) & 3) | ((L >> 4) << 2) and col(L) = ((L >> 3) & 1) * 4 + (L & 1) * 2, so out[2L + j] = 100 + 8 row(L) + col(L) + j, out[64 + 8r + c] names the lane and element that own (r, c), and the two views of r agree cell by cell. Every operand and partial sum is an integer below 2^24 (the largest product cell is 59964), so the result is exact whatever the accumulation order; a different ownership map, a transposed load or store, or elements 0 and 1 not being the multiply-add's operands all change the words. Nothing diverges and the AIR has no loop.

name: keep-the-longest-neighbour-velocity-that-points-the-way-it-came
rationale: neighborMaxVelocity has each thread scan the 3x3 tile neighbourhood of its own texel and keep the longest velocity whose direction is consistent with the offset it came from, and air.sign.v2f32 is the whole consistency test: it accepts a neighbour when |sign(i*vx) + sign(j*vy)| equals |clamp(i,-1,1)| + |clamp(j,-1,1)|. That makes the centre always count, an axis neighbour count whenever its on-axis velocity component is non-zero, and a diagonal neighbour count only when BOTH signs are non-zero and agree -- so a diagonal whose velocity points the wrong way is refused however long it is. The 48 velocities were searched for exactly that: 19 of the 48 threads reject a strictly longer neighbour on the sign test alone, so the answer is not the neighbourhood maximum and cannot be reached without evaluating the sign. Five separate ways of getting air.sign wrong each move at least 14 of the 48 texels: dropping the test entirely moves 19, returning the magnitude instead of the sign moves 14, returning +1 for zero instead of 0 moves 38, returning the operand unnormalised moves 27, and flipping only the x component's sign moves 21. One mutation the kernel cannot see is air.sign negated in BOTH components, because the test reads |a + b| and |(-a) + (-b)| is the same number; no case built on this host can distinguish that. Every value is exact. The velocity components are multiples of a half and the lengths are multiples of a quarter, all of them exactly representable and all 48 lengths distinct, so the strictly-greater comparison that drives the scan never sits on a tie; the offsets are -1, 0 and 1, so each product with a velocity is that velocity or zero; and the sums of signs and the clamped magnitudes are small integers, so the equality that gates acceptance is exact on both sides. searchRange is 1, and the static sampler the shader carries is nearest-filtered with pixel coordinates and clamp-to-edge, so the eight texels on each border resolve their off-texture taps back onto the edge and every one of the 48 threads is a full 3x3 scan. Every texel of the destination is written, and its fourth component is the constant 1 the shader puts there.

name: compare-an-argument-buffer-depth-texture-at-texel-centers-and-midpoints
rationale: DESIGN D285.10: thread g compares the 2x2 depth32_float texture of constant argument buffer 0 {depth2d<float> map;} at (0.25g, 0.25g), level 0, against 0.5 with the constexpr sampler shadow_less (normalized, linear, clamp to edge, compare less), through the heap's depth-comparison class, and writes the float to buffer 1. Rows are (0.25, 0.75), so column 1 passes (0.5 < 0.75) and column 0 fails. In texel space the coordinate is 0.5g - 0.5 on both axes: g = 0 clamps to texel (0, 0), g = 1 is its center, g = 2 is the midpoint of all four texels (weights 1/4 each), and g = 3 is the center of (1, 1). Every filter weight is 0, 1/4, 1/2 or 1, exact at any subtexel precision, so the results are exactly 0, 0, 0.5, 1.

name: sample-an-argument-buffer-texture-through-a-bound-pixel-sampler
rationale: DESIGN D285.14 and D73.3: thread g samples the 4x4 rgba32_float texture of constant argument buffer 0 {texture2d<float> t;} at pixel coordinate (0.25g, 0.25g), level 0, through the sampler bound at [[sampler(0)]] (pixel coordinates, nearest, clamp to edge), and writes the float4 to buffer 1. The engine normalizes a pixel coordinate by the element's level-0 size behind the slot's SamplerCoords specialization; the width 4 makes that division exact, so a coordinate on a texel edge (1, 2, 3) stays on it. Texel floor(0.25g) on both axes is read: texel (x, y) is (x + 4y, 0.5x, 0.25y, 1), so threads 4k to 4k + 3 write (5k, 0.5k, 0.25k, 1) for k = 0 to 3.

name: sample-an-argument-buffer-texture-through-a-bound-sampler
rationale: DESIGN D285.14: thread g samples the 3x3 rgba32_float texture of constant argument buffer 0 {texture2d<float> t;} at (0.25g, 0.25g), level 0, through the sampler bound at [[sampler(0)]] (normalized, nearest, clamp to edge), a heap sampler binding the binder writes with the bound sampler, and writes the float4 to buffer 1. Texel (x, y) is (x + 3y, 0.5x, 0.25y, 1). The width 3 keeps every coordinate off a texel edge: 3 * 0.25g is 0, 0.75, 1.5 and 2.25, texels (0, 0), (0, 0), (1, 1) and (2, 2), so the results are (0, 0, 0, 1) twice, (4, 0.5, 0.25, 1) and (8, 1, 0.5, 1).

name: dsm2-shuffle-more-past-the-thread-count-forty-two
rationale: DESIGN D278 and D154.4: a threadgroup of 42: simdgroup 0 is whole (every word defined), and simdgroup 1 has lanes 0-9, whose third quad has lanes 8 and 9 only. Inputs (A): in[g] = 0xA5000000 + 0x00010101 * (g + 1), a distinct word per thread, whose float bits and high half are normal numbers; src[L] = (L + 16) & 31 for even L and L ^ 2 for odd L, the broadcast lane src[32] = 20, the delta src[33] = 8, the modulo src[34] = 32, the quad mask src[35] = 2, the quad lane src[36] = 3, and the quad delta src[37] = 1. out[10g + i] is lane g's word i: simd_broadcast, simd_shuffle_rotate_down, simd_shuffle_and_fill_up (filling with ~v), simd_shuffle_and_fill_down (filling with ~v, modulo 32), quad_shuffle_xor, quad_broadcast, quad_shuffle_down, quad_shuffle_rotate_down, and simd_shuffle of v's bits as a float and of its high half as a half. Every thread writes all ten words. Compiled without fast math. The AIR has no loop.

name: depthwise-conv-grad-data-k4x4-s2x2-cfirst-writes-every-channel
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-work case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero sizes fail every thread's bounds check. User constant 124 = 0: channel axis 0 (coordinate (c, x, y, d)), no odd offsets, no gradient accumulation (the write goes to postfixPrimary_f); constant 112 = 0 (padding mode 0). The data gradient's size is (W, H, D, C) = (4, 4, 2, 3), the gradient's (2, 2, 2, 3), zero offsets. One threadgroup of 3x2x8 threads: gid.x is the channel, x0 = 2 gid.y, the depth is gid.z / H and y0 = 2 (gid.z mod H). Threads with y0 = 0 or 2 take the full-block path and write their 2x2 block; threads with y0 = 4 or 6 fail the full-block test and the edge path writes nothing (y0 is outside H). The coordinate's first component is c, so words 0 to 2 are written and words 3 to 5 keep the 0xab fill. The retained modules of the source callbacks the case links return constants (prefixSecondary_f and prefixTertiary_f 0.0; the only retained modules of those functions), so every product is 0.0 and every sum exactly +0.0 in any order; every writer of a word stores that same value, so the observed words do not depend on write order. The variant observes the loops, the bounds checks and the written coordinates through the linked writer (postfixPrimary_f, module aad641ec, table entry 1 at the coordinate's first component), not data-dependent arithmetic. The kernel has no loop over data (the 4x4 taps are unrolled).

name: linked-k299-vector-matrix-per-tensor-asymmetric-half-activation-float-scale
rationale: Reaching variant of ddbb8a5e (vector-matrix-multiply-per-tensor-zero-shape), whose zero shape and constants leave the kernel no work (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). It is WP-EVG's float variant f53027fb on this half-activation kernel of the same template: the same constants (the simdgroup-per-row path without matrix multiply-accumulate, one K split, a 128-element K tile, four simdgroups per threadgroup, two activation vectors, the partial-reduction tail on and kDiv4 off, asymmetric per-tensor A, the direct pD write), the same params and the same int8 A[r][k] = (5k + 3r) mod 7 - 3 (ARowBytes 300), over half B[x][k] = (3k + 2x) mod 5 - 2 (BRowBytes 600: rows of 300 halves). Two threadgroups of 128 lanes (grid 128x2) give rows tgid.y*4 + simdgroup, 0 to 7: rows 0 to 6 are below N = 7 and row 7 returns at the bound. Each row reduces K = 299 in float (each half B converted exactly): two 128-element main steps, the guarded tail to K4 = 296, then lane 0's 3-element remainder, each subtracting the zero point 1 read as int8 from table entry 1; simd_sum, times the scale 0.5 read as float from table entry 0, and lane 0 writes half pD[x*8 + r] (DRowBytes 16: rows of 8 halves). Every product (a - 1) * b is an integer of magnitude at most 8 and every partial sum an integer below 2400, so each sum is exact in float in any order, and each result, a multiple of 0.5 of magnitude below 1024, is exact in half. The 32 observed bytes are pD's 16 halves: 14 written once each by a single lane, halves 7 and 15 keeping the 0xab fill (row 7 writes nothing). Every loop is finite by these inputs: K = 299 bounds the reduction, N = 7 the rows, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

name: selected-pointer-across-two-buffers-becomes-a-selected-value
rationale:
A pointer selected between two DISTINCT device buffers, whose only uses are loads. Logical SPIR-V cannot select pointers whose roots are different descriptor variables, so `passes::resources::selected_load::materialize_interface_selected_loads` loads each arm and selects the VALUE while the binding transaction still owns the graph. Measured with per-function coverage against every cased source, this fixture reaches 6 functions no cased source reaches -- `arm_is_loadable`, `emit_arm_load`, `scalar_bits`, `find_uint`, `constant` and `fresh` -- which is the whole of that file's gap. Before it, exactly one of the 14,579 corpus sources produced a plan here, a 3,939-line kernel that is uncased; 49 sources reach the candidate filter and 48 of them lose it because the select has a use that is not a load.

Three near-misses, each measured, and each one is why the shape is what it is. `p = flag ? a : b` with `p[tid]` afterwards never reaches the rule: the index after the select is a non-load use, and the select folds away before the pass sees it. Both arms being offsets -- `flag ? (a+tid) : (b+tid)` -- does not reach it either; one arm has to be the bare descriptor root. And a struct pointee folds the select entirely. What does reach it is one arm offset into `a`, the other `b` itself, dereferenced directly.

The rewrite loads BOTH arms on every lane and selects afterwards, so every lane dereferences `a + tid`, `a + tid + 1` and `b`. `a` is nine words precisely so `a + tid + 1` is in bounds at tid 7 on the lanes that do not select it.

The answer is derived, not blessed. `pick` is 0,1,0,1,1,0,1,0, and `a[i] = 100 + 7i`, `b[0] = 9`. A lane that takes `a` answers `a[tid] + 3*a[tid+1]`; a lane that takes `b` answers `4*b[0] = 36`. So out is 36, 449, 36, 505, 533, 36, 589, 36. The weight 3 on the second load makes a swapped or duplicated arm visible on every `a` lane, and the `b` lanes are what observe the arm the module loads but the output would otherwise never show. The output buffer starts at 0xffffffff, which no arm can produce.

`loop_free`: no loop and no call. One threadgroup of eight threads, the length of `pick` and of the output.
